candidates.title: Matched TEA/TEOA benchmark
candidates.purpose: Test whether changing the amine from TEOA to TEA alone alters CO/H2 distribution in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform under intentionally unmatched conditions to maximize donor contrast.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 and GX012 motivate a cobalt-containing photocatalytic CO2-reduction comparison using TEOA and TEA. EV063 suggests medium can matter, so the proposal transfers this by changing donor identity while also allowing donor-driven medium differences to remain, treating any resulting product shift as additive-specific. EV081, EV045, and EV022 support measuring CO and H2 together and including simple catalytic context controls.

comparisons.inference: Any CO/H2 difference is taken as direct evidence that donor identity controls selectivity, even if donor substitution also changes medium behavior.

procedure: Assemble the P01 TEOA formulation from the supplied system description and prepare TEA and no-amine variants by copying the same nominal setup.
Run illuminated CO2 photocatalysis for all groups in parallel reactors without additional matching adjustments so the donor environments remain naturally distinct.
Analyze headspace by the same GC workflow for CO and H2, preferably at one endpoint and one interim sample.
Compare product amounts and CO/H2 ratios across groups and rank donor effects by absolute difference.
measurements: GC-detected CO amount
GC-detected H2 amount
CO/H2 ratio or selectivity descriptor
Qualitative note of visible instability or precipitation after reaction
candidates.supports: A reproducible difference between E01G01 and E01G02 in either CO/H2 ratio or both product amounts supports H01 and is interpreted as mainly caused by amine identity.
candidates.refutes: Near-identical CO and H2 outcomes for E01G01 and E01G02 refute a meaningful donor effect in this platform.
candidates.inconclusive: Large run-to-run scatter, strong signals in E01G03, or obvious formulation instability make the comparison inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-grounded P01 TEOA formulation as the starting benchmark. If exact numeric settings are missing, select them by a short pilot that maximizes total gas production in the TEOA case, then copy the same nominal settings to TEA and no-amine without further correction.
candidates.limitations: This design wrongly treats donor substitution as a single-variable test even though amine identity can alter medium composition, proton behavior, and CO2 interactions. It does not isolate mechanism and weakly controls background artifacts.

candidates.purpose: Check whether observed CO/H2 comes from the intended photocatalytic system and whether donor-specific backgrounds distort the TEA/TEOA comparison, using a compact control set.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV046, EV081, EV045, and GX008 support negative controls such as dark, Ar/no-CO2, and component omissions. The proposal transfers this logic to the P01 donor comparison and assumes that if the full system exceeds a small control set, remaining background pathways are negligible.

procedure: Prepare the full TEOA and TEA systems plus one dark, one Ar, and one no-cobalt control.
Run all groups with the same reactor format and analyze CO and H2 by the same GC method.
Compare control outputs to their corresponding full system and then compare the two full systems.
If controls are lower than the full systems, proceed to interpret the TEA/TEOA difference as intrinsic.

candidates.refutes: Controls close to the full systems refute the benchmark and imply donor comparison is not meaningful.
candidates.inconclusive: Mixed outcomes across controls or large donor-specific background signals make donor conclusions inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the same nominal settings as E01. If a control gives no detectable gas, no further optimization is needed. If all groups are near detection limits, increase irradiation time by pilot equally for every group until at least one full system exceeds blank noise.
candidates.limitations: Controls are incomplete because they do not cover all omissions for both amines, yet the design still treats them as sufficient. Multi-factor contrasts are present across some groups, but the card interprets them as decisive artifact checks anyway.

candidates.title: Donor amount series
candidates.purpose: Test whether any TEA/TEOA difference persists across donor loadings by sweeping donor amount and reading selectivity trends, assuming amount and identity can be merged into one practical causal factor.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV061 links TEOA proportion to CO2-reduction output and suggests donor concentration can alter performance. EV063 indicates medium composition affects CO/H2 in a CoCl2/bpy-related system. EV059 motivates applying such amount variation within the P01 TEOA/TEA comparison and interpreting the combined landscape as donor behavior.

procedure: Choose two donor loadings spanning a visible performance range by brief pilot in the TEOA system, then reuse the same nominal low and high levels for TEA.
Run the four illuminated CO2 photocatalysis groups with all other nominal settings unchanged.
Measure CO and H2 by the same GC workflow and compare both within-donor amount trends and cross-donor differences at each amount.
Use the resulting pattern to decide whether donor identity or donor amount is the stronger determinant.
measurements: GC-detected CO amount

candidates.supports: If TEA and TEOA remain separated at both low and high donor amounts, H01 is supported and the donor effect is treated as intrinsic rather than condition-dependent.
candidates.refutes: If changing donor amount dominates while TEA and TEOA overlap at one or both levels, H01 is refuted.
candidates.inconclusive: Crossing trends, strong instability, or poor signal at one loading make the identity conclusion inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Define low and high donor amounts by a short pilot that finds one underperforming and one stronger TEOA condition. Apply the same nominal low and high amounts to TEA without compensating for compositional differences, because identical nominal addition is assumed to create the fairest comparison.
candidates.limitations: This combines donor identity and medium perturbation issues and overinterprets nominally matched additions as chemically matched conditions. Two-point amount sampling can miss nonmonotonic behavior and cannot isolate mechanism.

candidates.title: TEA versus TEOA donor-side quenching comparison in the P01 baseline matrix
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes upstream photoredox observables under otherwise matched P01-like formulations, providing a covariate for any donor-dependent CO/H2 shift without claiming full mechanism.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV053 and EV065 support transferable fluorescence/UV-vis quenching logic in donor-containing photocatalytic cobalt systems; GX007 shows TEA-for-TEOA substitution can change photochemical behavior; EV011 supports that TEA and TEOA form different donor-derived radical species after quenching. Proposed transfer: adapt these observables to the matched P01 absorber-containing formulation, with cobalt-containing and cobalt-free references to separate donor-side from cobalt-side effects.

procedure: Prepare matched absorber-containing samples using the P01 baseline composition logic, changing only donor identity or cobalt-component presence across groups.
Record fluorescence and/or UV-vis responses under identical optical settings, including blanks for solvent and absorber-free backgrounds if needed for subtraction.

Compare donor-dependent quenching trends first in cobalt-free matrices, then in cobalt-containing matrices, and retain raw spectra and corrected Stern-Volmer-style summaries only if linearity is empirically adequate.
measurements: Steady-state fluorescence intensity or lifetime proxy of the absorber-containing sample under matched excitation
UV-vis spectral changes during donor addition or short irradiation exposure
Apparent quenching trend versus donor condition in cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matrices
Background absorbance/scattering from donor, solvent, g-C3N4, and cobalt-containing mixtures
candidates.supports: A reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in quenching observable under otherwise matched conditions, especially if the direction is consistent across repeats and not explained by simple optical background, supports H01 secondary explanation that donor identity changes upstream photoredox entry. If this covaries with later CO/H2 differences from the benchmark, it strengthens but does not prove a donor-photophysics contribution.
candidates.refutes: If TEA and TEOA give indistinguishable quenching behavior within calibrated detection limits in both cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matrices, a large donor-specific upstream quenching difference is disfavored as the main explanation for any product shift, though downstream proton or cobalt-state effects remain possible.
candidates.inconclusive: Strong scattering, overlapping absorbance, unstable baselines, or donor-dependent sample degradation that prevents reliable assignment makes the result inconclusive. A difference in quenching alone also cannot establish the active catalytic pathway or predict CO/H2 direction without catalytic correlation.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the same nominal absorber, solvent matrix, and cobalt-component presence as the verified P01 baseline. Because no exact optical recipe is supplied, pilot donor additions should set a range that changes signal measurably without complete quench or severe inner-filter artifacts. Accept Stern-Volmer treatment only over the empirically linear region; otherwise report descriptive matched-point comparisons.
candidates.limitations: This is a characterization proposal, not a catalytic readout. Signals may reflect absorber/donor or absorber/cobalt interactions without identifying the turnover-relevant species. In a heterogeneous g-C3N4 matrix, scattering and adsorption can confound fluorescence or UV-vis comparisons. Transfer from EV053, EV065, and GX007 is methodological, not proof that the same quenching route controls P01 selectivity.

candidates.title: Near-operando cobalt-state comparison under TEOA and TEA
candidates.purpose: Assess whether TEA and TEOA correlate with different cobalt oxidation or coordination signatures in the P01 primary system, narrowing whether donor identity changes the cobalt-containing catalytic manifold rather than only bulk assay conditions.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the CoCl2 plus bpy plus g-C3N4 plus TEOA formulation family closest to the target context. GX008 supports UV-vis, XAS, IR, Raman, and related operando-capable methods for homogeneous or mixed photocatalytic systems, while EV046 supports before/after and control logic but warns that recovered-state data alone are insufficient. Proposed transfer: use the P01 baseline and TEA comparator with matched catalyst-containing and catalyst-free references, prioritizing near-operando measurements over post-reaction-only inference.

candidates.supports: A reproducible donor-dependent cobalt-associated spectral difference under matched illuminated conditions, especially when absent or smaller before illumination, supports a link between donor identity and the cobalt-containing catalytic manifold. Correlation with catalytic CO/H2 changes would strengthen this interpretation.
candidates.refutes: If TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in cobalt-associated signatures before or during illumination within the method's resolution, a large donor-specific cobalt-state change is disfavored as the dominant explanation for product differences, though subtle states below detection or non-cobalt factors may remain.
candidates.inconclusive: Recovered-sample-only differences, unresolved overlapping features, or spectral changes equally present in cobalt-free backgrounds are inconclusive for cobalt-state assignment. Even a clear donor-dependent cobalt signal cannot by itself prove the active species, rate-limiting step, or causal path to CO versus H2.
candidates.parameter_selection: Because no exact operando settings are supplied, choose the method by availability and cobalt detectability: low-barrier UV-vis if features are visible, or specialist XAS/IR/Raman if needed. Use pilot scans to determine concentration/pathlength or collection time that gives unsaturated, reproducible spectra and a short illumination interval that changes signal without complete decomposition. Hold reactor, gas handling, and optical flux constant across donors.
candidates.limitations: In situ active-state identity for P01 is unresolved. Heterogeneous support and mixed solution/solid phases can blur cobalt assignments. Pre/post contrasts are inherently time-coupled and therefore descriptive rather than isolated causal tests. This card characterizes state correlation, not full mechanism.

candidates.title: 13CO2 origin check for CO under matched TEOA and TEA conditions
candidates.purpose: Determine whether CO detected in the matched donor comparison is CO2-derived under both donor identities, protecting the TEA/TEOA selectivity comparison against donor-specific carbon artifacts or background CO formation.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV021 shows TEOA can participate non-innocently yet isotope labeling can still verify CO2 origin; EV046, EV022, EV082, and GX008 support transferable use of negative controls and 13CO2 plus GC-MS in photocatalytic CO2 reduction studies. Proposed transfer: apply reproducible 13CO2 labeling to the P01 matched benchmark for both donors, alongside key benchmark negatives, and interpret origin separately from selectivity or mechanism.

candidates.supports: Detection of the labeled CO signature in both donor conditions, with the corresponding unlabeled reference pattern in the natural-abundance runs and little or no labeled CO in the negative control, supports the claim that observed CO in the donor comparison is genuinely CO2-derived. This validates interpreting donor-dependent CO changes as altered CO2-reduction output rather than obvious carbon-source artifact.
candidates.refutes: If CO detected in a donor condition lacks the expected labeled signature under 13CO2, or if similar labeled CO appears in the key negative control, the central TEA/TEOA CO comparison is undermined and donor-specific or assay-background artifacts become a stronger explanation.
candidates.inconclusive: Very low CO signal, overlapping mass fragments, memory effects, or inconsistent gas handling can make origin assignment inconclusive. Even a positive 13CO2 result does not explain why TEA and TEOA differ; it only bounds the carbon-source question.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the same matched formulation and illumination program as the verified benchmark. Because no isotope-analysis recipe is supplied, first calibrate GC-MS retention and fragment assignment with unlabeled and labeled CO standards or validated instrument checks, then choose a sampling volume and run time that detect the smallest benchmark CO signal without overload. If product is near detection limit, prioritize fewer well-controlled labeled runs over a broad matrix.
candidates.limitations: This card verifies product origin, not mechanism. A positive result cannot distinguish donor-photophysics, proton management, medium effects, or cobalt-state explanations. The negative control is not a perfectly matched single-factor test if only one donor identity is used there; conclusions from that contrast must stay bounded.

candidates.title: Matched donor quenching in P01
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes absorber-side quenching or bleaching behavior in the primary Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform while other formulation elements are held fixed.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors a TEOA-based CoCl2/bpy/g-C3N4 CO2-reduction formulation as P01. EV053 and GX007 show fluorescence or UV-vis can discriminate donor-dependent quenching behavior and that TEA substitution can change photochemical fading rates in another cobalt-containing photochemical system. EV011 supports TEA and TEOA as reductive quenchers that form distinct donor-derived radicals. GX008 supports inclusion of omission controls and bounded interpretation. Proposed transfer: apply these observables within P01 only as characterization of upstream photophysics, not proof of the full catalytic mechanism.

candidates.supports: Support for H02 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in quenching or bleaching direction within cobalt-containing P01, with the donor contrast larger than instrumental/background variation and directionally consistent with any independently observed catalytic selectivity change. Similar donor differences in no-cobalt references would indicate an absorber-side donor effect; stronger differences only when cobalt is present would suggest donor-sensitive cobalt-associated pathways.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against a mainly upstream donor-quenching explanation would be indistinguishable TEA and TEOA optical responses in the matched cobalt-containing P01 samples after background correction and calibration, especially if catalytic CO/H2 still differs under the same formulation. That outcome would shift weight toward downstream proton-transfer, substrate-binding, or catalyst-state explanations.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if scattering, inner-filter effects, donor absorbance, suspension instability, or uncontrolled pH/ionic-strength changes prevent reliable comparison; also inconclusive if donor differences appear only in multi-factor unmatched sample states or if optical changes cannot be separated from irreversible decomposition.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-defined P01 composition family as the chemical starting point but verify exact loadings and optical density from source or pilot rather than inventing values. Pilot by scanning sample dilution and path length until baseline absorbance and emission are within the linear detector range and g-C3N4 scattering does not saturate the signal. Use identical preparation age, mixing, and illumination dose across groups. If suspension measurements are unstable, pilot matched filtrate and suspension modes as separate sample states rather than mixing them in one contrast.
candidates.limitations: Steady-state optical changes can indicate donor-dependent quenching or bleaching but cannot by themselves assign the reduced cobalt species, quantify electron flux into catalysis, or prove causation for CO/H2 selectivity. Support effects in P01 may make absorber and cobalt contributions overlap. No-cobalt references do not recreate the full catalytic manifold. If multiple factors such as donor identity and pH drift co-vary, causal attribution remains limited.

candidates.title: Transient reduced-state comparison
candidates.purpose: Determine whether TEA and TEOA produce different transient reduced-state amplitudes or lifetimes in the primary P01 system, indicating altered electron-delivery dynamics into the cobalt-containing catalytic manifold.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV007, EV041, and EV018 show that TEOA can alter reduced-state formation or lifetime and that CO2 can change transient decay behavior in photocatalytic systems. EV005 supports transient absorption as a way to monitor electron-side kinetics while cautioning that some carriers are inferred indirectly. GX008 supports TAS and related in situ methods for photocatalytic systems. Proposed transfer: use transient spectroscopy in P01 to compare donor-dependent kinetic observables, with assignments kept provisional unless cross-checked by catalyst-free references.

Larger or longer-lived donor-enabled reduced populations for one amine would support altered upstream electron delivery into the catalytic manifold.

candidates.parameter_selection: Choose probe wavelengths and time windows by pilot spectra on the TEOA baseline and no-donor control, selecting regions with clear signal-to-noise and minimal lamp/scattering artifacts. Calibrate pump fluence below the regime where signal scales nonlinearly or sample damage appears. Keep preparation age, suspension density, and optical path identical across groups. If assignment is uncertain, report donor-dependent kinetic differences descriptively and avoid species-specific labels unless corroborated by no-cobalt or absorber-only references.
candidates.limitations: This experiment requires specialist instrumentation and may still yield ambiguous assignments in a supported heterogeneous system. TAS can reveal kinetic differences but not full mechanism, product origin, or exact cobalt structure. No-cobalt controls help but do not reconstruct the same interfacial environment. If donor identity also changes proton activity or medium properties, a single transient contrast cannot isolate pure electron-transfer causality.

candidates.title: Supplementary P02 quenching transfer
candidates.purpose: Use the more chemically defined homogeneous cobalt/Ru platform P02 as a supplementary test of whether TEA versus TEOA changes donor-side quenching behavior when support effects are minimized.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV065 provides a cobalt photocatalytic CO2-reduction platform with Ru photosensitizer and TEOA plus quenching evidence, making P02 suitable for a supplementary donor-substitution test. EV053 and EV077 support luminescence or UV-vis quenching as mechanistic probes in donor-containing cobalt-related photochemical systems. EV011 supports TEA and TEOA as reductive quenchers that form donor-derived radicals. Proposed transfer: hold the P02 catalyst and photosensitizer constant, substitute TEA for TEOA, and compare quenching directionality without claiming that absolute kinetics or mechanism are identical to P01.

Repeat the TEOA condition with 13CO2 and, where spectral quality remains acceptable, with D2O substitution of the aqueous component to test isotope-sensitive assignments.
Process spectra by subtraction against appropriate pre-illumination and component-matched references, then compare emergence, shift, persistence, and decay of donor-dependent bands across groups.
Link any donor-dependent bands to parallel catalytic samples only descriptively, avoiding assignment of a full pathway unless isotope and control behavior are internally consistent.
measurements: Time-resolved IR spectra under illumination for all groups.
Wavenumber positions, isotope shifts, and temporal evolution of donor-dependent bands.
Presence or absence of candidate bands in cobalt-present versus cobalt-absent references.
Qualitative correspondence between operando spectral changes and separately measured CO/H2 outputs from matched catalytic runs.
Signal-to-noise, reproducibility across repeat runs, and extent of band overlap; these data cannot by themselves establish a unique intermediate structure or the rate-determining step.
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in reaction-state IR features under otherwise matched conditions, combined with isotope behavior that bounds at least one donor-dependent feature as CO2-derived and/or hydrogen-involving, and control behavior showing that the feature is not fully explained by donor-only background. This would support donor-specific substrate/intermediate stabilization or adduct-associated chemistry without proving a unique structure.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be that TEA and TEOA show no reproducible donor-dependent reaction-state IR differences beyond baseline noise or generic medium effects, while isotope substitution fails to reveal bounded CO2-derived or hydrogen-sensitive features unique to one donor. That outcome would favor explanations centered elsewhere, such as quenching kinetics, cobalt-state changes not visible here, or uncontrolled catalytic variability.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if spectra are dominated by overlap, weak signals, or baseline drift; if only multi-factor changes can be interpreted; if isotope substitution broadly perturbs the system without clear assignment value; or if donor-dependent bands appear but cannot be separated from cobalt-free or dark backgrounds. In that case the experiment remains descriptive and cannot discriminate H05 from competing explanations.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent literature conditions. Use the source-verified P01 formulation where available; otherwise first pilot the IR cell with the reported TEOA baseline to find the highest concentration/path length/collection time that preserves unsaturated absorbance and stable baselines. Keep reactor geometry, illumination, gas flow or headspace protocol, and acquisition timing identical across TEA and TEOA. Introduce 13CO2 and D2O only after confirming the baseline condition gives reproducible transient bands. If D2O causes major formulation instability or gross rate collapse, retain it as a bounded assignment aid rather than a matched mechanistic test.
candidates.limitations: Transferred from non-Co systems and generic methods evidence. Band assignment may remain ambiguous because donor, solvent, support, cobalt-ligand, bicarbonate/carbonate, and product bands can overlap. D2O and 13CO2 can alter kinetics as well as frequencies. Near-operando measurements may miss the true operating state, and operando IR alone cannot prove primary quenching route, exact adduct identity, or that a detected species is on-path rather than spectator. The cobalt-absent control does not isolate support versus donor contributions separately.

candidates.source_to_proposal: EV021 motivates explicit isotope origin-bounding because CO was reported from CO2 rather than TEOA decomposition in a different TEOA-containing photochemical system. EV085 warns that donor decomposition and altered active species can confound product assignment. GX008 supports negative controls and reproducible 13CO2 labeling in photocatalytic CO2-reduction studies. EV063 shows that in a CoCl2/bpy-containing photocatalytic system, CO and H2 outputs are medium-sensitive, so the TEA/TEOA comparison should keep all non-donor factors matched. candidates.supports: Support for H05 is stronger if G01 and G02 show a reproducible donor-dependent difference in the CO2-derived 13CO fraction or 13CO/H2 ratio while inert-gas controls remain low for donor-derived background CO and the broader program finds no commensurate donor difference in upstream electron-supply observables. This would show that the TEA/TEOA effect is not merely an artifact of counting non-CO2 carbon as product, though it would still not prove adduct identity.
candidates.refutes: H05 is weakened if the apparent TEA/TEOA CO difference disappears once analysis is restricted to confirmed 13CO2-derived CO, or if donor-dependent CO appears similarly in inert-gas or dark controls, indicating that background chemistry can account for the prior selectivity difference. H05 is also weakened if 13CO/H2 remains indistinguishable between donors under well-matched conditions and controls.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if isotopic resolution is insufficient, baseline CO contamination or carryover is non-negligible, medium matching between TEA and TEOA is not credible, or any observed donor effect is comparable to run-to-run variability. A retained donor difference in 13CO origin confirms a real product-origin effect but still cannot distinguish adduct stabilization from cobalt-state or quenching explanations.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations, light dose, or runtime. Use the verified P01 baseline if explicitly available; otherwise run a pilot to choose a reaction duration that gives quantifiable CO and H2 above blank yet remains before obvious saturation or severe deactivation. Calibrate gas analysis with labeled and unlabeled CO standards or equivalent instrument checks, confirm no memory effect by blank injections, and use the same sampling cadence and reactor volume across all groups. If TEA substitution changes pH, conductivity, or phase behavior enough to break comparability, document this and either predefine a matched-medium adjustment pilot or treat the comparison as partially confounded rather than a strict single-factor test.
candidates.limitations: This candidate bounds carbon origin but does not directly observe amine-CO2 adducts, catalyst-linked intermediates, or operating cobalt speciation. TEA and TEOA can change multiple hidden properties even when nominal formulation is matched, including proton activity and solvation, so a donor effect here is not uniquely attributable to adduct stabilization. The dark control is intentionally limited and, if only one donor is used, becomes a multi-factor descriptive check rather than a donor-specific contrast. Transfer from the cited literature is methodological and cautionary, not direct proof for P01.

candidates.title: Matched TEA/TEOA integration of adduct-sensitive signals with quenching observables
candidates.purpose: Test whether donor-dependent substrate-associated or catalyst-linked signals persist between TEA and TEOA under otherwise matched Co-bpy photocatalysis even when donor-side quenching observables are similar, thereby discriminating H05 from a purely upstream quenching explanation.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV029 and GX011 provide transferable but non-Co evidence that TEOA can form catalyst/CO2-associated adduct chemistry beyond simple donation. EV011 supports the competing explanation that both TEA and TEOA can act through reductive quenching and donor-radical formation. GX008 supports combining negative controls, 13CO2 origin checks, and spectroscopy in homogeneous photocatalytic CO2-reduction studies. Proposed transfer: in the P01 Co-bpy baseline, compare TEA versus TEOA while holding the rest of the formulation fixed and integrate any adduct/intermediate-sensitive spectral difference with independently measured quenching behavior. This is a proposal, not a reported Co-bpy result.

candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in substrate-associated or catalyst-linked spectral signatures, and/or CO2-origin-bounded behavior linked to those signatures, while donor-side quenching observables remain similar enough that upstream quenching alone cannot account for the catalytic difference. candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be that under matched conditions TEA and TEOA show no reproducible difference in adduct/intermediate-sensitive signals beyond noise or assignment uncertainty, while any catalytic difference is instead accompanied by clear quenching differences large enough to explain it, or the TEA/TEOA product difference disappears after strict matching.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if both quenching and adduct-sensitive observables change together, if signal assignment is ambiguous, if isotope sensitivity is below detection, if products are too low for reliable integration, or if medium/property differences introduced by donor substitution alter multiple observables without isolating downstream substrate-associated chemistry.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations, path lengths, or irradiation settings. Start from the reported P01 TEOA formulation and verify exact values from supplied sources; if absent, run a calibration pilot that first matches absorbance/scattering window, catalyst detectability, and measurable CO/H2 formation for the baseline. Then choose acquisition timing where both quenching and spectral signals are above background but before obvious bulk decomposition or precipitation. Use the same donor molar role and the same total reaction volume across TEA and TEOA unless a preparatory solubility or medium-compatibility pilot shows this is not feasible; if not feasible, retain the comparison as partially confounded rather than pretending full matching.
candidates.limitations: Depends on prior establishment of a usable adduct-sensitive method and quenching assay in this platform. TEA and TEOA change more than one latent property of the medium, so even the primary contrast may combine donor, base, proton-management, and solvation effects. A spectral signal can indicate donor-dependent association or intermediate population but cannot alone establish the exact structure, rate-limiting step, or full catalytic pathway. 13CO2 controls bound product origin but do not prove that a specific observed signal is the productive intermediate.

procedure: Prepare the four matched P01 group formulations from the same component stocks and reactor setup, changing only the listed factor values and documenting pH or other medium covariates rather than assuming equality.

Expose each group to the assigned CO2 isotopic atmosphere, collect pre-illumination and illuminated operando or near-operando spectra using the same background and reference protocol, and run catalytic sampling on the same schedule.

Quantify at least CO and H2 for all groups with the same analytical workflow; if feasible, pair gas analysis with a targeted spectroscopic window chosen in a pilot for donor-sensitive changes under CO2.
Repeat the key TEA, TEOA, and no-amine groups sufficiently to check whether any donor-specific signature and product trend is reproducible rather than a single-run artifact.
measurements: Gas-phase CO and H2 from each group; if 13CO2 is used, isotopic composition of CO when detectable.
Operando or near-operando IR, Raman, UV-Vis, XAS, or other validated speciation signal selected by pilot for sensitivity to donor-dependent CO2-associated or catalyst-associated changes.
Pre-illumination versus illuminated spectra under matched backgrounds to distinguish pre-equilibrated adduct formation from light-dependent changes.
Medium covariates needed for comparability, such as pH or other donor-induced bulk changes, noting that these covariates do not establish identical local chemistry.

If a donor-specific spectroscopic feature appears, its presence or absence across groups; the signal can indicate association or state change but cannot alone prove a complete catalytic pathway or exact structure without independent assignment support.
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible CO2-associated spectroscopic feature or isotopically bounded behavior present with TEOA but absent in both TEA and no-amine groups, or substantially stronger with TEOA while upstream electron-supply observables remain similar in the matched comparison. Additional support would be TEOA-specific changes in CO/H2 output that track that signature across repeats.
candidates.refutes: Evidence would weigh against H05 if TEA and TEOA show no meaningful difference in the targeted signatures or 13CO2-bounded behavior under matched conditions, and any catalytic differences are absent or better aligned with bulk medium changes or known quenching differences rather than donor-specific CO2-associated states. A complete loss of the original TEA/TEOA selectivity difference under stricter controls would also weaken the hypothesis.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if signals are below detection, poorly assigned, not reproducible, or changed together with uncontrolled covariates such as amine-induced medium shifts. Similar product outputs with insufficient spectroscopic sensitivity, or donor-specific spectra without validated relation to catalysis, also remain non-discriminating.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations, irradiation settings, or acquisition windows. Use the reported P01 formulation where explicitly supplied; otherwise verify from source records or run a pilot that first identifies a stable baseline with detectable CO and H2 and a measurable donor-sensitive spectral region. For TEA substitution, start with the same nominal donor role used in the baseline and document any bulk-property mismatch. If signal saturation or no signal occurs, adjust only the analytical acquisition settings or sample path length before changing chemistry. Use 13CO2 only after natural-abundance runs show sufficient CO signal for isotopic discrimination.
candidates.limitations: TEA and TEOA differ simultaneously in donor, base, coordination, and medium effects, so even a single-factor formulation change does not isolate one microscopic cause. Cross-system literature on Re or other catalysts motivates but does not prove analogous Co-bpy adducts. No-amine controls may strongly suppress catalysis, limiting comparison to necessity rather than selectivity. Spectroscopic assignments may be ambiguous without orthogonal confirmation, and recovered-sample measurements may miss the operating state.

candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible donor-specific substrate-associated signal under CO2 where TEOA and TEA differ, combined with evidence that the key feature requires cobalt or is accompanied by donor-specific cobalt coordination/state changes under otherwise matched conditions. Stronger support would come from agreement across at least two independent observables.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be no reproducible donor-specific substrate-associated difference after matched controls, or donor-specific signals that are fully reproduced in no-cobalt references with no parallel cobalt-state change, making catalyst-linked adduct or intermediate stabilization unnecessary for explaining the TEA/TEOA difference.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive outcomes include weak or overlapping signals, donor-dependent bulk medium effects that obscure cobalt features, multi-feature changes that cannot be assigned uniquely, or differences seen only in recovered or dark samples. Such outcomes may still justify bounded descriptive conclusions but not a catalyst-linked adduct claim.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations, irradiation settings, or spectral windows. Use the source-verified P01 recipe where available; otherwise run a small pilot to match absorbance/scattering baselines, confirm spectrometer dynamic range, and choose acquisition timing around the earliest reproducible catalytic window identified in prerequisite experiments. Accept a method only if the donor comparison can be collected with identical cell geometry, gas handling, and background subtraction for all groups.
candidates.limitations: Direct Co-bpy TEA/TEOA adduct evidence is absent from the supplied record, so this is a transfer test. g-C3N4 and mixed medium can create background bands and heterogeneous broadening. A donor effect on cobalt-sensitive observables may reflect coordination, aggregation, decomposition, or support association rather than a discrete CO2 adduct. No-cobalt controls do not fully reproduce the chemical environment of cobalt-containing samples, so absence of a feature there is supportive but not definitive.
